plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids or strategies. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks losses if I win at a higher price, while bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, and given the theoretical guarantee that truthful bidding maximizes expected profit in second-price auctions, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniform on [0,49]. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid truthfully, equal to your value. Bidding your true value ensures that if you win, you pay the second-highest bid, and your profit is always non-negative. Bidding higher risks paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since there's no history to suggest deviation, I will bid exactly my value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value only risks negative profit, and bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform beliefs about opponents' strategies, and since truthful bidding is weakly dominant in this format, I will bid exactly my value of $13.
